Gold.note: Central bank accumulation and macroeconomic hedging support elevated prices.

Silver.note: Strong dual precious and industrial demand drivers alongside gold's momentum.

Copper.note: Tight concentrate markets and structural green energy transition demand.

Uranium.note: Structural primary supply deficit and renewed global nuclear capacity additions.

Lithium.note: Near-term oversupply and moderating EV battery demand growth pressure margins.

Nickel.note: Persistent surplus class 2 nickel supply from Indonesia weighs on the market.

Zinc.note: Record low smelter treatment charges indicate severely tight concentrate supply.

Iron Ore.note: Ongoing structural weakness and stimulus limits in China's property sector.

Coal.note: Resilient near-term thermal demand offset by long-term energy transition risks.

Rare Earths.note: Geopolitical supply risks balanced by sluggish high-tech manufacturing demand.

Manganese.note: Weak global steel production margins dampen ferroalloy demand.

PGM.note: Deep underground supply constraints in South Africa offsetting sluggish auto demand.

Potash.note: Normalizing global supply chains perfectly balance steady agricultural fertilizer demand.

Aluminum.note: Strict capacity caps in China and strong lightweight automotive demand.

Diversified.note: Balanced exposure to copper and iron ore provides a hedge against single-commodity volatility.
